title: Daily SGS Top 5
tagline: Five stories, one question: who's in control?

stories.headline: Nigeria asks World Bank for a $500M loan
stories.summary: Nigeria asked the World Bank for a $500M loan to launch INFRAGROW. Approval is set for May 2027, adding to debt near $121B.
stories.label: Moderately Globalist
stories.why: More of Nigeria's building plans would run on a lender's terms.
stories.what_it_means: Nigeria's building plans would run on a lender's terms.
stories.economic_impact: The loan would add to public debt already about $121B; repayment falls on future taxpayers.
stories.everyday_example: It's like putting a new roof on a credit card where the bank picks the contractor.

stories.headline: US skips its UN human rights review again
stories.summary: The US is skipping its UN human rights review in Geneva for the second year, the first country to skip it completely.
stories.label: Slightly Sovereign
stories.why: Washington will not let a UN panel grade it.
stories.what_it_means: Washington will not let a UN panel grade it.
stories.economic_impact: Little market effect, but it signals a wider walk away from UN bodies.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a homeowner who quit the HOA turning away its inspector.

stories.headline: Novaya Gazeta shuts its Moscow office
stories.summary: Novaya Gazeta, Russia's last big independent paper, closed its Moscow office after a foreign-agent label, blocked donations, and an editor's arrest.
stories.label: Strongly Globalist
stories.why: The state shut the last big newsroom that questioned it.
stories.what_it_means: The state shut the newsroom that questioned it at home.
stories.economic_impact: Readers lose a free source as those donations dry up.
stories.everyday_example: It's like the town paper getting locked out after the mayor froze its tip jar.

stories.headline: Iran and Qatar float a Hormuz reopening plan
stories.summary: Iran's leader ordered an end to the standoff, and Qatar brought a plan to reopen Hormuz. The US would lift a blockade and free part of $8B if Hormuz reopens with Oman for tankers. Iran denies any swap, and a deal is not close.
stories.label: Moderately Globalist
stories.why: Tehran still wants to decide who sails the strait.
stories.what_it_means: Tehran still wants to decide who sails the strait.
stories.economic_impact: Shipping and fuel costs stay high; about a fifth of the world's oil used to pass Hormuz.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a neighbor offering to reopen the only road if he sets the toll lane.

stories.headline: US floats redrawing Ukraine's map
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi talks opened; the US floated redrawing Ukraine's map so Moscow can claim the Donbas on paper while Ukraine keeps Sloviansk and Kramatorsk. Zelensky refuses to give up land.
stories.label: Strongly Globalist
stories.why: Outside powers are sketching a nation's borders.
stories.what_it_means: Outside powers are sketching a nation's borders.
stories.economic_impact: Europe rejected a plan to bring Russian gas back, which would ease the squeeze but rebuild dependence.
stories.everyday_example: It's like two neighbors redrawing your property line so one of them can say he won.
